A couple of things I'd need to actually confirm the numbers:
- Which AWS account owns these instances (could be a different member account in your org)
- Real per-instance max/peak CPU, not just the average — a fleet that averages 9% but spikes to 70% on some instances needs a more conservative resize than one that's uniformly flat

That said, here's the ballpark using public us-east-1 on-demand Linux pricing (not pulled live — I hit a permissions gap on the Pricing API, so treat this as directional):

| Instance type | ~$/hr | ~$/mo each | 40 instances/mo |

| m5.xlarge (half) | $0.192 | ~$140 | ~$5,600 |
| m5.large (quarter) | $0.096 | ~$70 | ~$2,800 |

At a consistent 9% average CPU, m5.2xlarge → m5.xlarge is a safe, conservative call (doubles utilization to ~18%, still comfortable headroom) and would save roughly **$5,600/month** across the 40 instances. If the workload is genuinely flat with no spiky instances, you could potentially go two sizes down to m5.large (~18% → ~36% effective utilization), saving closer to **$8,400/month** — but I wouldn't recommend that without confirming peak/p99 CPU per instance first, since a few spiky instances in that batch could get starved.
